claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you have.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you're inquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18 years old, there are specific rules that apply to Child Benefit for children aged 16 and over.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and isn't doing anything formal right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question to confirm:

**Is Alex currently in paid work, and if so, how many hours per week is he working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just been at home since finishing school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the rules, Child Benefit normally continues for children aged 16-19 only if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is 18 years old and is not currently in approved education or training, and is not working, he does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit eligibility.

Additionally, the rules state that you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, Alex is already 18, so this exception would not apply.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- Alex is 18 years old
- Child Benefit normally ends when a child reaches 16, unless they remain in approved education or training
- Since Alex is not currently in education or training, he does not meet the eligibility requirements

If Alex does decide to pursue education, training, or registers with a careers service in the future, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again - so it's worth keeping this in mind if his circumstances change.
